newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Zeitler urges ECB to adopt money supply aim.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Zeitler urges ECB to adopt money supply aim.

text.p: Europe's future central bank should adopt a money supply target, at least at the beginning, Bundesbank council member Franz-Christoph Zeitler said on Wednesday.

At the beginning, "a money supply target and a perspective on inflation can lend the new central bank additional transparency and credibility," Zeitler, also president of the state central bank in Bavaria, said.
Zeitler warned against adopting an inflation target, which some nations have used with mixed success to steer monetary policy. Germany currently uses M3 money supply growth to guide policy.
"A central bank can only indirectly impact prices while it is better able to impact money supply growth," Zeitler said.
Some economists believe money supply growth foreshadows future inflation developments.
Equally undesirable would be a monetary policy based on foreign exchange rate targets, Zeitler said.

Zeitler also warned that the European Central Bank (ECB) must be vigilant about making price stability its foremost goal. The euro must become the stability anchor for other currencies and adopt the mark's role as an international reserve currency.
